issues.summary: The bulk replace left `if (app) await app?.close()` inside an existing `if (app)` guard, so the optional chaining does nothing.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: feature-flag.service.integration.spec.ts:23 and messages.controller.integration.spec.ts:50 both wrap `app?.close()` in `if (app)`. The `?.` is redundant but harmless, so this only affects style.

issues.summary: `app?.close()` is used on a local `const app` that was just created and initialised, so it can never be undefined there.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: feature-flag.service.integration.spec.ts:86-97: `const app = await new TestAppProvider().provide(...)` followed by `await app.init()`, so the `?.` at line 97 has no effect. This is harmless churn.

issues.summary: No deterministic test covers the name.builder truncation fix (or the bridge-name resample), so reverting either would only show up as a rare flake.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: name.builder.ts:28 adds a second sanitizeName after the slice, and only the existing randomized idempotence test exercises it. The code under test is a test builder, so a regression would only bring back a CI flake and would not affect production behaviour.

issues.summary: The bridge-name resample `while` loop has no upper bound.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: bridge-name.entity.spec.ts:21-24 loops while `isBridgeName(name)`. faker's noun list is far larger than the roughly 20 bridge names and the seeded sequence is deterministic, so the loop will not realistically run forever.

issues.summary: The claim is that re-sanitizing after truncation could drop the name below NAME_MIN_LENGTH.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: name.builder.ts:25-28: truncation only happens to strings longer than NAME_MAX_LENGTH (30), and trimming the trailing whitespace of a 30-code-point slice of an already-sanitized name cannot plausibly bring it under the minimum. The finding itself admits this case is unreachable.
